sanskrit: candrārkānilavahnīnāṃ kāntidīptibaladyutīḥ yau sadā bibhratur vīrau tāv imau keśavārjunau
english: These two heroes, Keśava and Arjuna, who forever bear the loveliness of the moon, the blaze of the sun, the force of the wind, and the splendour of fire.

sanskrit: brahmeśānāv ivājayyau vīrāv ekarathe sthitau sarvabhūtavarau vīrau naranārāyaṇāv ubhau
english: Unconquerable as Brahmā and Īśāna, the two heroes stood upon a single chariot — the foremost of all beings, the two heroes who are Nara and Nārāyaṇa.

sanskrit: ity etan mahad āścaryaṃ dṛṣṭvā śrutvā ca bhārata aśvatthāmā susaṃyattaḥ kṛṣṇāv abhyadravad raṇe
english: Beholding and hearing of this great wonder, O Bhārata, Aśvatthāman, fully girded, rushed upon the two Kṛṣṇas in battle.

sanskrit: atha pāṇḍavam asyantaṃ yamakālāntakāñ śarān seṣuṇā pāṇināhūya hasan drauṇir athābravīt
english: Then, as the son of Pāṇḍu was loosing arrows like Yama, Time, and the Ender, the son of Droṇa hailed him with arrow-laden hand, and laughing spoke.

sanskrit: yadi māṃ manyase vīra prāptam arham ivātithim tataḥ sarvātmanādya tvaṃ yuddhātithyaṃ prayaccha me
english: "If, O hero, you reckon me come to you as a guest deserving of welcome, then with all your soul grant me this day the hospitality of battle."

sanskrit: evam ācāryaputreṇa samāhūto yuyutsayā bahu mene 'rjuno ''tmānam idaṃ cāha janārdanam
english: Thus challenged by the teacher's son with desire for combat, Arjuna held himself in high honour, and said this to Janārdana:

sanskrit: saṃśaptakāś ca me vadhyā drauṇir āhvayate ca mām yad atrānantaraṃ prāptaṃ praśādhi tvaṃ mahābhuja
english: "The Saṃśaptakas too are mine to slay, and the son of Droṇa now summons me. O mighty-armed one, instruct me which of these is to be met first."

sanskrit: evam ukto 'vahat pārthaṃ kṛṣṇo droṇātmajāntikam jaitreṇa vidhināhūtaṃ vāyur indram ivādhvare
english: So addressed, Kṛṣṇa bore Pārtha into the presence of Droṇa's son — as the Wind bears Indra summoned by victorious rite into the sacrifice.

sanskrit: tam āmantryaikamanasā keśavo drauṇim abravīt aśvatthāman sthiro bhūtvā praharāśu sahasva ca
english: Addressing him with single mind, Keśava said to Droṇa's son: "Aśvatthāman, stand firm, strike swiftly, and endure!"

sanskrit: nirveṣṭuṃ bhartṛpiṇḍaṃ hi kālo 'yam upajīvinām sūkṣmo vivādo viprāṇāṃ sthūlau kṣātrau jayājayau
english: "This is the hour for dependants to repay the bread of their lord. Subtle is the dispute of brāhmaṇas; gross are the victory and defeat of the kṣatriya."

sanskrit: yāṃ na saṃkṣamase mohād divyāṃ pārthasya satkriyām tām āptum icchan yudhyasva sthiro bhūtvādya pāṇḍavam
english: "Since out of folly you cannot brook the divine welcome Pārtha would do you, then, desiring to win it, stand firm this day and fight the son of Pāṇḍu."

sanskrit: ity ukto vāsudevena tathety uktvā dvijottamaḥ vivyādha keśavaṃ ṣaṣṭyā nārācair arjunaṃ tribhiḥ
english: So addressed by Vāsudeva, the best of the twice-born said "So be it," and pierced Keśava with sixty iron shafts and Arjuna with three.

sanskrit: tasyārjunaḥ susaṃkruddhas tribhir bhallaiḥ śarāsanam cicchedāthānyad ādatta drauṇir ghorataraṃ dhanuḥ
english: At this Arjuna, sorely enraged, severed his bow with three broad-headed arrows; whereupon Droṇa's son took up another, still more terrible, bow.

sanskrit: sajyaṃ kṛtvā nimeṣāt tad vivyādhārjunakeśavau tribhiḥ śarair vāsudevaṃ sahasreṇa ca pāṇḍavam
english: Stringing it in the blink of an eye, he pierced Arjuna and Keśava — Vāsudeva with three arrows and the son of Pāṇḍu with a thousand.

sanskrit: tataḥ śarasahasrāṇi prayutāny arbudāni ca sasṛje drauṇir āyastaḥ saṃstabhya ca raṇe 'rjunam
english: Then, straining himself, Droṇa's son loosed arrows by the thousand, by the million, by the hundred million, and in the battle held Arjuna in check.

sanskrit: iṣudher dhanuṣo jyāyā aṅgulībhyaś ca māriṣa bāhvoḥ karābhyām uraso vadanaghrāṇanetrataḥ
english: From his quiver, his bow, his bowstring, his fingers, O honoured one, from his arms, his two hands, his breast, his face, his nostrils, his eyes,

sanskrit: karṇābhyāṃ śiraso 'ṅgebhyo lomavartmabhya eva ca rathadhvajebhyaś ca śarā niṣpetur brahmavādinaḥ
english: from his two ears, his head, his limbs, even from the very pores of his skin, and from his chariot and banner, the arrows of that reciter of the Veda streamed forth.

sanskrit: śarajālena mahatā viddhvā keśavapāṇḍavau nanāda mudito drauṇir mahāmeghaughanisvanaḥ
english: Having pierced Keśava and the son of Pāṇḍu with a vast net of arrows, Droṇa's son roared in delight with a voice like a mass of great thunderclouds.

sanskrit: tasya nānadataḥ śrutvā pāṇḍavo 'cyutam abravīt paśya mādhava daurātmyaṃ droṇaputrasya māṃ prati
english: Hearing him roar, the son of Pāṇḍu said to Acyuta: "Behold, Mādhava, the malice of Droṇa's son toward me."

sanskrit: vadhaprāptau manyate nau praveśya śaraveśmani eṣo 'sya hanmi saṃkalpaṃ śikṣayā ca balena ca
english: "Having shut us within a house of arrows, he thinks us slain; this resolve of his I shall undo by skill and by strength."

sanskrit: aśvatthāmnaḥ śarān astāṃś chittvaikaikaṃ tridhā tridhā vyadhamad bharataśreṣṭho nīhāram iva mārutaḥ
english: Cutting each of the arrows loosed by Aśvatthāman into three and three, the best of the Bharatas scattered them as the wind scatters mist.

sanskrit: tataḥ saṃśaptakān bhūyaḥ sāśvasūtarathadvipān dhvajapattigaṇān ugrair bāṇair vivyādha pāṇḍavaḥ
english: Then the son of Pāṇḍu once more pierced the Saṃśaptakas — with their horses, drivers, chariots, and elephants, their banners and bands of foot — with fierce arrows.

sanskrit: ye ye dadṛśire tatra yad yad rūpaṃ yathā yathā te te tat tac charair vyāptaṃ menire ''tmānam eva ca
english: Whoever there beheld any form, in whatever wise, each thought that form, and his own self, all covered over with arrows.

sanskrit: te gāṇḍīvapraṇuditā nānārūpāḥ patatriṇaḥ krośe sāgre sthitān ghnanti dvipāṃś ca puruṣān raṇe
english: Sped from the Gāṇḍīva, those winged shafts of many shapes struck down elephants and men standing a full krośa away in the battle.

sanskrit: bhallaiś chinnāḥ karāḥ petuḥ kariṇāṃ madakarṣiṇām chinnā yathā paraśubhiḥ pravṛddhāḥ śaradi drumāḥ
english: Severed by broad-headed arrows, the trunks of the rut-streaming elephants fell, like full-grown autumn trees felled by axes.

sanskrit: paścāt tu śailavat petus te gajāḥ saha sādibhiḥ vajrivajrapramathitā yathaivādricayās tathā
english: And thereafter those elephants fell like mountains, together with their riders, even as ranges of hills shattered by the thunderbolt of the Thunderer.

sanskrit: gandharvanagarākārān vidhivat kalpitān rathān vinītajavanāny uktān āsthitān yuddhadurmadān
english: The chariots, fashioned by rule and like to the cities of the Gandharvas, drawn by horses trained to swiftness and well-guided, mounted by warriors mad for battle —

sanskrit: śarair viśakalīkurvann amitrān abhyavīvṛṣat alaṃkṛtān aśvasādīn pattīṃś cāhan dhanaṃjayaḥ
english: these Dhanaṃjaya rained his foes with arrows, hewing them to splinters, and slew the bedecked horsemen and the foot-soldiers.

sanskrit: dhanaṃjayayugāntārkaḥ saṃśaptakamahārṇavam vyaśoṣayata duḥśoṣaṃ tīvraiḥ śaragabhastibhiḥ
english: Dhanaṃjaya, the sun of the world's ending, dried up the great, unfordable ocean of the Saṃśaptakas with the fierce rays of his arrows.

sanskrit: punar drauṇimahāśailaṃ nārācaiḥ sūryasaṃnibhaiḥ nirbibheda mahāvegais tvaran vajrīva parvatam
english: Then again, with swift, sun-bright iron shafts of mighty force, he hastened to cleave the great mountain that was Droṇa's son, as the Thunderer cleaves a hill.

sanskrit: tam ācāryasutaḥ kruddhaḥ sāśvayantāram āśugaiḥ yuyutsur nāśakad yoddhuṃ pārthas tān antarācchinat
english: The teacher's son, enraged and eager to fight, sought with swift arrows to strike him together with his horses and driver, but could not, for Pārtha cut the shafts down in mid-air.

sanskrit: tataḥ paramasaṃkruddhaḥ kāṇḍakośān avāsṛjat aśvatthāmābhirūpāya gṛhān atithaye yathā
english: Then Aśvatthāman, exceedingly enraged, loosed whole sheaves of arrows upon the worthy Arjuna — as one offers a house to a guest.

sanskrit: atha saṃśaptakāṃs tyaktvā pāṇḍavo drauṇim abhyayāt apāṅkteyam iva tyaktvā dātā pāṅkteyam arthinam
english: Then, leaving the Saṃśaptakas, the son of Pāṇḍu fell upon Droṇa's son — as a giver leaves an unworthy man to attend a worthy suppliant.

sanskrit: tataḥ samabhavad yuddhaṃ śukrāṅgirasavarcasoḥ nakṣatram abhito vyomni śukrāṅgirasayor iva
english: Then there arose a combat between those two, splendid as Śukra and Aṅgiras — like Venus and the planet of Aṅgiras around a star in the sky.

sanskrit: saṃtāpayantāv anyonyaṃ dīptaiḥ śaragabhastibhiḥ lokatrāsakarāv āstāṃ vimārgasthau grahāv iva
english: Scorching each other with the blazing rays of their arrows, they stood, striking terror into the worlds, like two planets straying from their courses.

sanskrit: tato 'vidhyad bhruvor madhye nārācenārjuno bhṛśam sa tena vibabhau drauṇir ūrdhvaraśmir yathā raviḥ
english: Then Arjuna pierced him sorely between the brows with an iron shaft; and Droṇa's son shone thereby like the sun with rays flung upward.

sanskrit: atha kṛṣṇau śaraśatair aśvatthāmnārditau bhṛśam saraśmijālanikarau yugāntārkāv ivāsatuḥ
english: Then the two Kṛṣṇas, sorely afflicted by Aśvatthāman with hundreds of arrows, stood with their masses of beams entangled, like two suns at the world's ending.

sanskrit: tato 'rjunaḥ sarvatodhāram astram; avāsṛjad vāsudevābhiguptaḥ drauṇāyaniṃ cābhyahanat pṛṣatkair; vajrāgnivaivasvatadaṇḍakalpaiḥ
english: Then Arjuna, guarded by Vāsudeva, loosed the weapon that strikes on every side, and smote the son of Droṇa with shafts like the thunderbolt, like fire, like the rod of Yama.

sanskrit: sa keśavaṃ cārjunaṃ cātitejā; vivyādha marmasv atiraudrakarmā bāṇaiḥ sumuktair atitīvravegair; yair āhato mṛtyur api vyatheta
english: He of surpassing fire and most fearsome deeds pierced Keśava and Arjuna in their vital parts with well-loosed arrows of utmost speed, by which even Death, if struck, would tremble.

sanskrit: drauṇer iṣūn arjunaḥ saṃnivārya; vyāyacchatas tad dviguṇaiḥ supuṅkhaiḥ taṃ sāśvasūtadhvajam ekavīram; āvṛtya saṃśaptakasainyam ārchat
english: Warding off the arrows of the straining Droṇa's son with twice as many fair-feathered shafts, Arjuna enveloped that lone hero with his horses, driver, and banner, and then turned upon the Saṃśaptaka host.

sanskrit: dhanūṃṣi bāṇān iṣudhīr dhanurjyāḥ; pāṇīn bhujān pāṇigataṃ ca śastram chatrāṇi ketūṃs turagān athaiṣāṃ; vastrāṇi mālyāny atha bhūṣaṇāni
english: Their bows, their arrows, their quivers, their bowstrings, their hands, their arms, the weapons held in their hands, their parasols, their banners, their horses, their garments, their garlands, and their ornaments —

sanskrit: carmāṇi varmāṇi manorathāṃś ca; priyāṇi sarvāṇi śirāṃsi caiva ciccheda pārtho dviṣatāṃ pramuktair; bāṇaiḥ sthitānām aparāṅmukhānām
english: their shields, their armour, their cherished hopes, all that was dear to them, and their very heads — Pārtha clove asunder with the arrows he loosed at his foes, who stood without turning their faces away.

sanskrit: sukalpitāḥ syandanavājināgāḥ; samāsthitāḥ kṛtayatnair nṛvīraiḥ pārtheritair bāṇagaṇair nirastās; tair eva sārdhaṃ nṛvarair nipetuḥ
english: The well-equipped chariots, horses, and elephants, mounted by manful heroes who strove with effort, struck down by the hosts of arrows Pārtha sped, fell together with those best of men.

sanskrit: padmārkapūrṇendusamānanāni; kirīṭamālāmukuṭotkaṭāni bhallārdhacandrakṣurahiṃsitāni; prapetur urvyāṃ nṛśirāṃsy ajasram
english: Faces fair as lotuses, as the sun, as the full moon, splendid with diadems, garlands, and crowns — smitten by broad-heads, crescent-arrows, and razor-shafts, the heads of men fell ceaselessly to the earth.

sanskrit: atha dvipair devapatidvipābhair; devāridarpolbaṇamanyudarpaiḥ kaliṅgavaṅgāṅganiṣādavīrā; jighāṃsavaḥ pāṇḍavam abhyadhāvan
english: Then with elephants like the elephant of the lord of the gods, swelling with the pride and wrath of the foes of the gods, the heroes of the Kaliṅgas, Vaṅgas, Aṅgas, and Niṣādas, seeking to slay him, charged upon the son of Pāṇḍu.

sanskrit: teṣāṃ dvipānāṃ vicakarta pārtho; varmāṇi marmāṇi karān niyantṝn dhvajāḥ patākāś ca tataḥ prapetur; vajrāhatānīva gireḥ śirāṃsi
english: The armour, the vital parts, the trunks, and the drivers of those elephants Pārtha rent apart; and their banners and pennons then fell down like the peaks of a mountain struck by the thunderbolt.

sanskrit: teṣu prarugṇeṣu guros tanūjaṃ; bāṇaiḥ kirīṭī navasūryavarṇaiḥ pracchādayām āsa mahābhrajālair; vāyuḥ samudyuktam ivāṃśumantam
english: When these were broken, the Diademed one covered the teacher's son with arrows the hue of the new-risen sun — as the wind veils the toiling sun with great nets of cloud.

sanskrit: tato 'rjuneṣūn iṣubhir nirasya; drauṇiḥ śarair arjunavāsudevau pracchādayitva divi candrasūryau; nanāda so 'mbhoda ivātapānte
english: Then, beating off Arjuna's arrows with his own, Droṇa's son covered Arjuna and Vāsudeva with shafts as the moon and sun are veiled in the sky, and roared like a raincloud at the end of the hot season.

sanskrit: tam arjunas tāṃś ca punas tvadīyān; abhyarditas tair avikṛttaśastraiḥ bāṇāndhakāraṃ sahasaiva kṛtvā; vivyādha sarvān iṣubhiḥ supuṅkhaiḥ
english: Sorely pressed by him and by your warriors, whose weapons were yet unbroken, Arjuna made at once a darkness of arrows and pierced them all with fair-feathered shafts.

sanskrit: nāpy ādadat saṃdadhan naiva muñcan; bāṇān raṇe 'dṛśyata savyasācī hatāṃś ca nāgāṃs turagān padātīn; saṃsyūtadehān dadṛśū rathāṃś ca
english: Neither taking up, nor nocking, nor loosing his arrows could Savyasācin be seen in the battle; men saw only the slain elephants, horses, foot-soldiers, and chariots, their bodies sewn through with shafts.

sanskrit: saṃdhāya nārācavarān daśāśu; drauṇis tvarann ekam ivotsasarja teṣāṃ ca pañcārjunam abhyavidhyan; pañcācyutaṃ nirbibhiduḥ sumuktāḥ
english: Nocking ten choice iron shafts in haste, Droṇa's son loosed them as though they were but one; and of these, five well-sped shafts struck Arjuna and five pierced Acyuta.

sanskrit: tair āhatau sarvamanuṣyamukhyāv; asṛkkṣarantau dhanadendrakalpau samāptavidyena yathābhibhūtau; hatau svid etau kim u menire 'nye
english: Struck by these, those two foremost of all men, streaming blood, like Kubera and Indra, seemed overcome by one whose lore was complete; and others wondered, "Are these two slain?"

sanskrit: athārjunaṃ prāha daśārhanāthaḥ; pramādyase kiṃ jahi yodham etam kuryād dhi doṣaṃ samupekṣito 'sau; kaṣṭo bhaved vyādhir ivākriyāvān
english: Then the lord of the Dāśārhas said to Arjuna: "Why are you heedless? Slay this warrior! Neglected, he will work mischief, and grow grievous as a malady left untreated."

sanskrit: tatheti coktvācyutam apramādī; drauṇiṃ prayatnād iṣubhis tatakṣa chittvāśvaraśmīṃs turagān avidhyat; te taṃ raṇād ūhur atīva dūram
english: Saying "So be it" to Acyuta, and now alert, he hewed at Droṇa's son with arrows in earnest; and cutting the reins, he struck the horses, which bore him far away from the battle.

sanskrit: āvṛtya neyeṣa punas tu yuddhaṃ; pārthena sārdhaṃ matimān vimṛśya jānañ jayaṃ niyataṃ vṛṣṇivīre; dhanaṃjaye cāṅgirasāṃ variṣṭhaḥ
english: Wheeling about, that wise one, best of the line of Aṅgiras, desired no further combat with Pārtha; for, reflecting, he knew that victory was assured to the Vṛṣṇi hero and to Dhanaṃjaya.

sanskrit: pratīpakāye tu raṇād aśvatthāmni hṛte hayaiḥ mantrauṣadhikriyādānair vyādhau dehād ivāhṛte
english: When Aśvatthāman of hostile frame had been borne off from the battle by his horses — as a disease is driven from the body by spells, herbs, treatment, and gifts —

sanskrit: saṃśaptakān abhimukhau prayātau keśavārjunau vātoddhūtapatākena syandanenaughanādinā
english: Keśava and Arjuna advanced together to face the Saṃśaptakas, upon their chariot, its banner tossed by the wind, thundering like a flood.

sanskrit: saṃjaya uvāca athottareṇa pāṇḍūnāṃ senāyāṃ dhvanir utthitaḥ rathanāgāśvapattīnāṃ daṇḍadhāreṇa vadhyatām
english: Saṃjaya said: Then to the north, in the army of the Pāṇḍavas, an uproar arose from chariots, elephants, horses, and foot-soldiers being slaughtered by Daṇḍadhāra.

sanskrit: nivartayitvā tu rathaṃ keśavo 'rjunam abravīt vāhayann eva turagān garuḍānilaraṃhasaḥ
english: Turning the chariot back, Keśava, even as he urged on the horses swift as Garuḍa and the wind, said to Arjuna:

sanskrit: māgadho 'thāpy atikrānto dviradena pramāthinā bhagadattād anavaraḥ śikṣayā ca balena ca
english: "The lord of Magadha too has pressed forward upon his crushing elephant, in no way inferior to Bhagadatta in skill and in strength."

sanskrit: enaṃ hatvā nihantāsi punaḥ saṃśaptakān iti vākyānte prāpayat pārthaṃ daṇḍadhārāntikaṃ prati
english: "When you have slain him, you shall slay the Saṃśaptakas again." And at the end of his words he brought Pārtha into the presence of Daṇḍadhāra.

sanskrit: sa māgadhānāṃ pravaro 'ṅkuśagraho; graheṣv asahyo vikaco yathā grahaḥ sapatnasenāṃ pramamātha dāruṇo; mahīṃ samagrāṃ vikaco yathā grahaḥ
english: That chief of the Māgadhas, his goad in hand, irresistible among adversaries as a comet among the planets, that dreadful one churned the enemy's host as a flaming comet would scourge the whole earth.

sanskrit: sukalpitaṃ dānavanāgasaṃnibhaṃ; mahābhrasaṃhrādam amitramardanam rathāśvamātaṅgagaṇān sahasraśaḥ; samāsthito hanti śarair dvipān api
english: Mounted upon his well-caparisoned elephant — like a Dānava-elephant, roaring like a great cloud, a crusher of foes — he slew chariots, horses, and herds of elephants by the thousand, and elephants too, with his arrows.

sanskrit: rathān adhiṣṭhāya savājisārathīn; rathāṃś ca padbhis tvarito vyapothayat dvipāṃś ca padbhyāṃ caraṇaiḥ kareṇa ca; dvipāsthito hanti sa kālacakravat
english: Bearing down upon the chariots with their horses and drivers, in haste he ground the chariots beneath the elephant's feet; and mounted on the elephant he slew other elephants with its legs, its feet, and its trunk, like the wheel of Time.

sanskrit: narāṃś ca kārṣṇāyasavarmabhūṣaṇān; nipātya sāśvān api pattibhiḥ saha vyapothayad dantivareṇa śuṣmiṇā; saśabdavat sthūlanaḍān yathā tathā
english: And men decked in armour of black iron, with their horses, together with the foot-soldiers, he cast down and crushed with his furious, noble tusker, as one tramples thick reeds with a crackling sound.

sanskrit: athārjuno jyātalaneminisvane; mṛdaṅgabherībahuśaṅkhanādite narāśvamātaṅgasahasranāditai; rathottamenābhyapatad dvipottamam
english: Then Arjuna, amid the twang of bowstring, the slap of the leather guard, and the rim's roar, amid the din of drums, kettledrums, and many conches, and the clamour of men, horses, and elephants by the thousand, swept down upon that noble elephant on his peerless chariot.

sanskrit: tato 'rjunaṃ dvādaśabhiḥ śarottamair; janārdanaṃ ṣoḍaśabhiḥ samārdayat sa daṇḍadhāras turagāṃs tribhis tribhis; tato nanāda prajahāsa cāsakṛt
english: Then Daṇḍadhāra smote Arjuna with twelve choice arrows, Janārdana with sixteen, and the horses with three apiece; and thereupon he roared and laughed again and again.

sanskrit: tato 'sya pārthaḥ saguṇeṣukārmukaṃ; cakarta bhallair dhvajam apy alaṃkṛtam punar niyantṝn saha pādagoptṛbhis; tatas tu cukrodha girivrajeśvaraḥ
english: Then Pārtha with his broad-headed arrows cut away his bowstring, his arrows, and his bow, and his bedecked banner too, and again the drivers along with the foot-guards; and at this the lord of Girivraja flew into a rage.

sanskrit: tato 'rjunaṃ bhinnakaṭena dantinā; ghanāghanenānilatulyaraṃhasā atīva cukṣobhayiṣur janārdanaṃ; dhanaṃjayaṃ cābhijaghāna tomaraiḥ
english: Then, seeking to throw Arjuna into utter confusion with his elephant, its temples burst with rut, dense as a thundercloud and swift as the wind, he smote Janārdana and Dhanaṃjaya with lances.

sanskrit: athāsya bāhū dvipahastasaṃnibhau; śiraś ca pūrṇendunibhānanaṃ tribhiḥ kṣuraiḥ praciccheda sahaiva pāṇḍavas; tato dvipaṃ bāṇaśataiḥ samārdayat
english: Then the son of Pāṇḍu, with three razor-shafts, severed at one stroke his two arms, like elephant trunks, and his head, with its face like the full moon; and thereafter he smote the elephant with hundreds of arrows.

sanskrit: sa pārthabāṇais tapanīyabhūṣaṇaiḥ; samārucat kāñcanavarmabhṛd dvipaḥ tathā cakāśe niśi parvato yathā; davāgninā prajvalitauṣadhidrumaḥ
english: That elephant, clad in golden mail, shone with Pārtha's arrows tipped with refined gold, and so blazed as at night a mountain blazes, its herbs and trees set alight by a forest fire.

sanskrit: sa vedanārto 'mbudanisvano nadaṃś; calan bhraman praskhalito ''turo dravan papāta rugṇaḥ saniyantṛkas tathā; yathā girir vajranipātacūrṇitaḥ
english: Tormented with pain, trumpeting with a voice like a thundercloud, staggering, reeling, stumbling, stricken, in flight, broken, that elephant fell together with its driver, as a mountain falls crushed by the descent of the thunderbolt.

sanskrit: himāvadātena suvarṇamālinā; himādrikūṭapratimena dantinā hate raṇe bhrātari daṇḍa āvrajaj; jighāṃsur indrāvarajaṃ dhanaṃjayam
english: When his brother had been slain in battle, Daṇḍa came on upon an elephant white as snow, garlanded with gold, and like the peak of the snowy mountain, seeking to slay Dhanaṃjaya, the younger brother of Indra.

sanskrit: sa tomarair arkakaraprabhais tribhir; janārdanaṃ pañcabhir eva cārjunam samarpayitvā vinanāda cārdayaṃs; tato 'sya bāhū vicakarta pāṇḍavaḥ
english: Striking Janārdana with three lances bright as the sun's rays and Arjuna with five, he roared as he tormented them; then the son of Pāṇḍu hewed off his two arms.

sanskrit: kṣuraprakṛttau subhṛśaṃ satomarau; cyutāṅgadau candanarūṣitau bhujau gajāt patantau yugapad virejatur; yathādriśṛṅgāt patitau mahoragau
english: Cleanly cut off by razor-arrows, the two arms, still grasping their lances, their armlets fallen, smeared with sandal-paste, falling together from the elephant, gleamed like two great serpents tumbling from a mountain crag.

sanskrit: athārdhacandreṇa hṛtaṃ kirīṭinā; papāta daṇḍasya śiraḥ kṣitiṃ dvipāt tac choṇitābhaṃ nipatad vireje; divākaro 'stād iva paścimāṃ diśam
english: Then the head of Daṇḍa, struck off by the Diademed one with a crescent-arrow, fell from the elephant to the earth; and that blood-red head, as it fell, gleamed like the sun sinking from his setting-place toward the western quarter.

sanskrit: atha dvipaṃ śvetanagāgrasaṃnibhaṃ; divākarāṃśupratimaiḥ śarottamaiḥ bibheda pārthaḥ sa papāta nānadan; himādrikūṭaḥ kuliśāhato yathā
english: Then Pārtha pierced the elephant, like the peak of a white mountain, with choice arrows bright as the sun's rays; and it fell trumpeting, as a peak of the snowy mountain falls when struck by the thunderbolt.

sanskrit: tato 'pare tatpratimā gajottamā; jigīṣavaḥ saṃyati savyasācinam tathā kṛtās tena yathaiva tau dvipau; tataḥ prabhagnaṃ sumahad ripor balam
english: Then other noble elephants like to that one, seeking in the fray to conquer Savyasācin, were made by him even as those two elephants had been; and thereupon the foe's vast host was shattered.

sanskrit: gajā rathāśvāḥ puruṣāś ca saṃghaśaḥ; parasparaghnāḥ paripetur āhave parasparapraskhalitāḥ samāhatā; bhṛśaṃ ca tat tat kulabhāṣiṇo hatāḥ
english: Elephants, chariots, horses, and men in throngs, slaying one another, fell in the battle, stumbling against one another and struck down; and calling out their several clan-names, they were sorely slain.

sanskrit: athārjunaṃ sve parivārya sainikāḥ; puraṃdaraṃ devagaṇā ivābruvan abhaiṣma yasmān maraṇād iva prajāḥ; sa vīra diṣṭyā nihatas tvayā ripuḥ
english: Then his own soldiers, gathering about Arjuna as the hosts of the gods about Purandara, said: "He of whom we went in dread, as creatures dread death — that foe, O hero, by good fortune you have slain!"
